## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`slugify` needs fixing because it treats accented and other non-ASCII letters as separators, so it does not behave as the description says. The PR description also needs the `## Testing` section that project policy requires.

## Changes
This pull request adds `app/slug.py` with a regex-based `slugify(title)` that builds page URLs from titles. It also adds a parametrized test in `tests/test_slug.py` covering ASCII, padded, hyphen-only and empty titles.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters in slugs — The title `"Café au lait"` becomes `"caf-au-lait"`, and `"日本語"` becomes `""`. The cause is that `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as non-alphanumeric. This contradicts the PR body, which says only "runs of non-alphanumeric characters" are replaced. — Pages with non-English titles get truncated URLs, or empty ones that collide with each other. — Fix: Either match Unicode word characters, for example `re.sub(r"[\W_]+", "-", title.lower())`, or transliterate first with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)`, then add a non-ASCII case to `test_slugify`.
- PR body — correctness — Add a `## Testing` section to the description — The PR description has no `## Testing` section. It contains only one sentence about what `slugify` does. This breaks the rule "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." (`AGENTS.md:4`). — Maintainers cannot tell from the description whether or how the change was verified.
